references.text: God promises Abraham that his offspring will be as numerous as the dust on the earth, a precursor to the promise in 15:5 that his offspring will be like the stars in the sky.
God's promise to Abraham that his descendants will be as numerous as the stars and as the sand on the seashore repeats and expands upon the promise from 15:5.
God repeats the promise to Isaac that his offspring will become as numerous as the stars in the sky, a direct continuation of the promise given to Abraham in 15:5.
Moses reminds God of the promise made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to make their offspring as numerous as the stars, a direct reference back to the promise in Gen 15:5.
Moses states that the Lord has made the Israelites as numerous as the stars, demonstrating the fulfillment of the promise in Gen 15:5.
The Lord counts the stars and calls them by name, underscoring God's omnipotence—the same God who promised Abraham an offspring as numerous as the stars.
Paul describes how Abraham believed against hope that he would become the father of many nations, in accordance with the promise regarding his offspring, linking this to justification by faith.
Paul explains that the promises given to Abraham and his offspring point to Christ, and that all who belong to Christ are Abraham's offspring and heirs according to the promise.
The book of Hebrews describes how from one man, Abraham, descendants were born as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore, in line with God's promise.
Repetition and confirmation of the same promise regarding numerous descendants and nations.
Confirmation of the same covenant: Abraham will become the father of a multitude of nations and kings.
Historical fulfillment of the promise: The children of Israel became as numerous as the stars in the sky.
Theological explanation of Abraham's response to the promise concerning the stars: complete conviction in God's power.
